LESSON: SIGN READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE SIGN READING: INDEPENDENT READING AND SIGN READING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read widely? ● Why should we sign read widely? ● What materials do you enjoy reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words and phrases related to the theme, Nutrition-balanced diet,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. sign read a variety of familiar materials independently to build sign reading speed and fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply appropriate strategies to read and sign read independently for information and enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the importance of independent reading and sign reading in lifelong learning. ● In pairs, learners are guided to watch a captioned video clip or observe a signed demonstration of vocabulary related to nutrition. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to nutrition. ● In groups, learners are guided to select age - appropriate and high- interest reading materials such as narratives, poems, newspapers and magazines in print or electronic format. ● In groups, learners are guided to set up an after-school club where they meet on a regular basis and read, and sign read varied texts. ● In groups, learners are guided to retell by signing the stories they have read collaboratively. ● In groups, learners are guided to share opinions and reflections on the texts they have read or sign read. ● In groups, learners are guided to use materials in the classroom to read or sign read extensively. ● In groups, learners are guided to read, and sign read texts quietly or silently for pleasure. ● Why should we read widely? ● Why should we sign read widely? ● What materials do you enjoy reading? 42

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Independent Reading and sign reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learner uses selected reading materials from electronic sources.

• Learning to learn: Learn independently as learner develops extensive reading strategies in their language clubs.

Values:
● Responsibility: is cultivated as the learner engages diligently in assigned duty.

● Love: the learner respects other learners' opinions when reading.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to link the concept of reading to Kiswahili, English language ,Science and Technology ,Social Studies Mathematics, Integrated

Science, Agriculture and Nutrition, Religious Education, Creative Arts.

Suggested learning resources:

Word cards, Chart, Class readers, Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g. tablets, mobile phone, Dictionary, Internet, Signed audio-visual

recordings, Posters, Pictures and Photographs ,Extracts from newspapers, magazines and books, E-books, Internet, Online dictionaries, Digital story

books, Projector, Computers or Digital devices with internet

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. recognize signs of words and phrases related to the theme, Nutrition-balanced diet,
2. select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,
3. sign read a variety of familiar materials independently to build sign reading speed and fluency,
4. apply appropriate strategies to read and sign read independently for information and enjoyment,
